analysis.title: GS What Matters Today: Monster beat by SK Hinyx, All eyes on Microsoft/Google, Macro Assets in Fed Hiking Cycles
key_insights: SK Hynix (000660 KS) beat on Q3 profit by a wide margin and reaffirmed HBM shortages through at least 2030. Shares +10%. Revenue +32% sequentially, operating profit +38%, margins at 80%.
More than half of SK Hynix 2027/28 capacity is already under long term agreements.
Financing concerns around AI have begun to abate this week. The demand side never changed. The debate was about supply, financing and a risk reduction exercise across the Street.
The prior two weeks included some of the lowest net exposures all year and among the largest two week institutional tech liquidations on record.

Early signs of offense appeared yesterday, with buying in parts of the semi complex and some demand for upside vol. Investors have barely begun to re-risk. What has been seen is abatement of supply, not meaningful fresh demand.
A big beat being rewarded is reassuring for the AI trade.

Microsoft and Google earnings matter. Buyside expectations are closer to Azure growth in the high 40s% and Google Cloud growth around the mid 90s%. The question is whether results surpass already high expectations.

Azure probably needs a guidance raise to be properly supportive. If a miss comes only from limited compute capacity, it hurts near term revenue but is potentially more bullish for the scarcity premium and future spending.
Watch customer concentration, breadth of demand, and the relationship between revenue growth, capex and margins. The market wants evidence that incremental economics work.

Across nine Fed tightening cycles since the early 1980s, equities tended to struggle initially after the first hike but recover quickly. Yields rose into the first hike and rose further after it in larger cycles. The curve kept flattening, especially in larger cycles. The real trade-weighted USD tended to strengthen into the hike, with mixed performance afterwards.

GS baseline of a modest number of hikes, growth around potential and gradual inflation relief points to a modestly positive path for equities. Risk scenarios are an earlier end to tightening on better inflation news (most positive for risk assets), an interruption from growth or financial stress (less friendly at first), or a longer cycle if growth stays resilient (raises risk of a larger growth downgrade later).
